title: Consumer contract scope
text_en: The protective consumer-contract rules apply where the trader pursues or directs commercial activities to the consumer's Member State in the circumstances specified by this provision.

title: Jurisdiction for consumer contracts
text_en: A consumer may sue the other contracting party either in the courts of that party's Member State of domicile or, regardless of that party's domicile, in the courts for the place where the consumer is domiciled.

title: Jurisdiction for consumer contracts
text_en: The other contracting party may sue a consumer only in the courts of the Member State in which the consumer is domiciled.

title: Choice-of-court limits in consumer contracts
text_en: A choice-of-court agreement in a consumer contract may depart from the protective jurisdiction rules only under the conditions stated in this provision.

title: Employer actions against employees
text_en: An employer generally may bring proceedings against an employee only in the courts of the Member State in which the employee is domiciled.

title: Exclusive jurisdiction
text_en: Article 24 assigns exclusive jurisdiction, regardless of the parties' domicile, for the listed subject matters.

title: Exclusive jurisdiction
text_en: Proceedings whose object is rights in rem in, or tenancies of, immovable property are generally within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State where the property is situated, subject to the stated short private-tenancy exception.

title: Validity of companies and corporate decisions
text_en: Proceedings principally concerned with the validity, nullity, or dissolution of a company or the validity of decisions of its organs are within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State in which the company has its seat.

title: Exclusive jurisdiction
text_en: Proceedings whose object is the validity of entries in public registers are within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State in which the register is kept.

title: Validity of registered intellectual property
text_en: Proceedings concerned with the registration or validity of patents, trade marks, designs, or other similar rights required to be deposited or registered fall within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State in which the deposit or registration has been applied for, has taken place, or is deemed to have taken place, irrespective of whether the issue is raised by way of an action or as a defence.

title: Enforcement of judgments
text_en: Proceedings concerned with enforcement of judgments are within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State in which enforcement takes place or is sought.

title: Choice-of-court agreements
text_en: Article 25 governs agreements conferring jurisdiction on a court or the courts of a Member State.

title: Choice-of-court agreements
text_en: A choice-of-court agreement satisfying the stated formal and substantive conditions confers jurisdiction on the designated Member State court and is exclusive unless the parties agree otherwise.

title: Choice-of-court agreements
text_en: Electronic communication that provides a durable record of a jurisdiction agreement is equivalent to writing.

title: Choice-of-court agreements
text_en: A jurisdiction agreement has no legal force if it conflicts with the specified protective-jurisdiction provisions or purports to exclude a court having exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24.

title: Appearance without jurisdiction objection
text_en: Apart from jurisdiction derived from other provisions of the Regulation, a court of a Member State before which a defendant enters an appearance has jurisdiction, except where the appearance was entered to contest jurisdiction or another court has exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24.

title: Jurisdiction by appearance
text_en: For specified weaker parties, jurisdiction based on appearance requires the court to ensure that the defendant was informed of the right to contest jurisdiction and of the consequences of appearing or not appearing.

title: Own-motion review of exclusive jurisdiction
text_en: When the courts of another Member State have exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24, the court seised must declare of its own motion that it has no jurisdiction.

title: Default of appearance
text_en: If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

title: Default of appearance
text_en: In the default-of-appearance situation, the court must stay proceedings until the defendant received the initiating document in time to defend or all necessary service steps were taken.

title: Default of appearance
text_en: The EU service-of-documents rule identified in this paragraph replaces Article 28(2) when the initiating document had to be transmitted between Member States under that instrument.

title: Default of appearance
text_en: Where the specified EU service instrument does not apply, the identified Hague Service Convention rule applies if the initiating document had to be transmitted abroad.

title: Same cause and same parties
text_en: Where courts of different Member States are seised of proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties, a court other than the court first seised must stay proceedings of its own motion and later defer if the first court's jurisdiction is established.

title: Mandatory stay for same cause and parties
text_en: Where proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties are brought in different Member States, a court other than the court first seised must stay its proceedings of its own motion.

title: Same cause and same parties
text_en: On request, a court seised of the dispute must promptly inform another seised court of the date on which it was seised under Article 32.

title: Same cause and same parties
text_en: Once the jurisdiction of the court first seised is established, every other court must decline jurisdiction in favour of that court.

title: Related actions
text_en: Article 30 governs related actions pending in courts of different Member States and distinguishes discretionary stay from conditional decline.

title: Related actions
text_en: When related actions are pending in courts of different Member States, a court other than the court first seised may stay its proceedings.

title: Related actions
text_en: While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

title: Related actions
text_en: Actions are related when they are so closely connected that hearing them together is expedient to avoid irreconcilable judgments from separate proceedings.

title: Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
text_en: Article 31 addresses competing exclusive-jurisdiction claims and priority for a court designated by an exclusive choice-of-court agreement; it is distinct from Articles 29 and 30.

title: Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
text_en: Without prejudice to Article 26, where a court designated by an exclusive Article 25 agreement is seised, any court of another Member State must stay proceedings until the designated court declares that it has no jurisdiction under the agreement.

title: Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
text_en: Once the court designated in the agreement establishes jurisdiction, every court of another Member State must decline jurisdiction in its favour.

title: When a court is deemed seised
text_en: The time when a court is deemed seised depends on lodging the initiating document with the court or the authority responsible for service, provided the claimant takes the required subsequent steps.

title: Related proceedings pending in a third State
text_en: A Member State court may stay proceedings in favour of related proceedings pending in a third State where the specified conditions, including avoidance of irreconcilable judgments, are satisfied.

title: General jurisdiction by defendant domicile
text_en: A person domiciled in a Member State is generally sued in the courts of that Member State, irrespective of nationality.

title: Enforcement procedure
text_en: Subject to the Regulation, enforcement procedure is governed by the law of the Member State addressed, and an enforceable judgment is enforced there under the same conditions as a domestic judgment.

title: Enforcement procedure
text_en: Grounds for refusing or suspending enforcement under the law of the Member State addressed apply only so far as they are compatible with the grounds specified in the Regulation.

title: Limits on derogation from domicile jurisdiction
text_en: A defendant domiciled in a Member State may be sued in another Member State only under the special rules listed in the Regulation.

title: Defendant not domiciled in a Member State
text_en: Article 6 addresses jurisdiction over defendants not domiciled in a Member State, principally by reference to Member State law subject to specified Regulation exceptions.
keywords: not domiciled in any EU Member State

title: Defendant outside all Member States
text_en: Where a defendant is not domiciled in a Member State, jurisdiction is generally determined by the law of the Member State court seised, subject to specified exceptions.
keywords: no domicile in the European Union

title: Defendant not domiciled in a Member State
text_en: Against a defendant not domiciled in a Member State, a person domiciled in a Member State may invoke that State's jurisdiction rules on the same basis as its nationals.
keywords: not domiciled in any EU Member State

title: Domicile of natural persons
text_en: Article 62 determines which domestic law a court applies when deciding whether a natural person is domiciled in a Member State.

title: Domicile of natural persons
text_en: To determine whether a party is domiciled in the Member State whose courts are seised, the court applies its own internal law.
keywords: no domicile in the European Union

title: Domicile of natural persons
text_en: If a party is not domiciled in the seised court's Member State, the court applies the law of another Member State to determine whether the party is domiciled there.

title: Domicile of companies and legal persons
text_en: For purposes of the Regulation, a company or other legal person is domiciled at its statutory seat.

title: Domicile of companies and legal persons
text_en: For purposes of the Regulation, a company or other legal person is domiciled at its central administration.

title: Domicile of companies and legal persons
text_en: For purposes of the Regulation, a company or other legal person is domiciled at its principal place of business.

title: Domicile of companies and legal persons
text_en: To determine whether a trust is domiciled in the seised court's Member State, the court applies its private-international-law rules.

title: Special jurisdiction
text_en: In matters relating to a contract, a defendant domiciled in a Member State may be sued in another Member State at the place of performance of the obligation in question.

title: Sale and service performance place
text_en: For a sale of goods, Article 7(1)(b) uses the place where the goods were or should have been delivered; for services, it uses the place where the services were or should have been provided.

title: Place of harmful event
text_en: In matters relating to tort or delict, proceedings may be brought in the courts for the place where the harmful event occurred or may occur.

title: Branch or establishment
text_en: A dispute arising out of the operations of a branch, agency, or other establishment may be brought in the courts for the place where it is situated.

title: Special jurisdiction
text_en: A qualifying dispute against a settlor, trustee, or beneficiary may be brought in the courts of the Member State in which the trust is domiciled.

instrument_title: Regulation (EU) 2017/1001 on the European Union trade mark
title: EU trade mark court jurisdiction
text_en: EU trade mark courts have exclusive jurisdiction over counterclaims for revocation or for a declaration of invalidity of an EU trade mark under Article 128.

instrument_title: Regulation (EU) 2017/1001 on the European Union trade mark
title: Counterclaims for revocation or invalidity
text_en: A counterclaim for revocation or for a declaration of invalidity may rely only on grounds for revocation or invalidity stated in the Regulation.

instrument_title: Regulation (EU) 2017/1001 on the European Union trade mark
title: Coordination with other actions
text_en: A national court dealing with an EU-trade-mark action other than an action listed in Article 124 must treat the EU trade mark as valid.

instrument_title: Regulation (EU) 2017/1001 on the European Union trade mark
title: Application for revocation or invalidity
text_en: An application for revocation or for a declaration of invalidity of an EU trade mark may be submitted to the European Union Intellectual Property Office by the persons and groups specified in this paragraph.
